cards.front: What should you know about shoulder joint?
cards.back: Ball-and-socket joint allowing a wide range of movement including flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation and circumduction.

cards.front: What should you know about elbow joint?
cards.back: Hinge joint allowing only flexion and extension.

cards.front: What should you know about hip joint?
cards.back: Ball-and-socket joint allowing flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation and circumduction.

cards.front: What should you know about knee joint?
cards.back: Hinge joint (modified) allowing primarily flexion and extension, with slight rotation when flexed.

cards.front: What should you know about abduction?
cards.back: = moving a limb away from the midline of the body. Adduction = moving a limb towards the midline of the body.

cards.front: What should you know about ankle joint?
cards.back: Hinge joint allowing plantar flexion (pointing foot down) and dorsiflexion (pulling foot up).

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — movement analysis in sport?
cards.back: 1. For Movement Analysis in Sport questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Movement Analysis in Sport to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

cards.front: What does Flexion at shoulder mean?
cards.back: Moving the arm forwards and upwards (e.g. Anterior deltoids, pectorals)

cards.front: What does Extension at shoulder mean?
cards.back: Moving the arm backwards and downwards (e.g. Latissimus dorsi, posterior deltoids)

cards.front: What does Abduction at shoulder mean?
cards.back: Moving the arm away from the body sideways (e.g. Deltoids (middle fibres))

cards.front: What does Adduction at shoulder mean?
cards.back: Moving the arm towards the body from the side (e.g. Pectorals, latissimus dorsi)

cards.front: What does Flexion at elbow mean?
cards.back: Bending the elbow, decreasing the angle (e.g. Biceps (agonist), brachialis)

cards.front: What does Extension at elbow mean?
cards.back: Straightening the elbow, increasing the angle (e.g. Triceps (agonist))

cards.front: What does Flexion at hip mean?
cards.back: Lifting the leg forwards and upwards (e.g. Iliopsoas (hip flexors), rectus femoris)

cards.front: What does Extension at hip mean?
cards.back: Moving the leg backwards (e.g. Gluteals, hamstrings)
